Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does a low surrogate score prove a good package?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Check fidelity and domain.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A search algorithm may find designs where a surrogate is inaccurate rather than designs that are physically better. Trace the visual in order: search pressure; model blind spot; verification. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: If a candidate sits outside the model's training range, mark it out of domain and run a higher-fidelity check.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: If a candidate sits outside the model's training range, mark it out of domain and run a higher-fidelity check. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
